clue.text: Hound graduate's group of acquaintances

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, stands for a graduate; the 's is a link
a set is a social circle of people who know one another

explanation.surface: A dog owner's description of the hound belonging to someone who has just graduated, or that graduate's circle of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged scent dog, a breed in the hound group.

clue.text: Advanced to cut off old spacecraft

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
to poll a tree or animal is to cut off its top or horns

explanation.surface: A news item about an old spaceship, once ahead of its time, being scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo missions used the craft that carried astronauts to the Moon.

clue.text: Club in which I dry old-fashioned receptacle

indicators.note: in which places the remaining letters inside the club word

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's club where someone dries a vintage container.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a crossword convention for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a bowl for spitting into, common in earlier times.

clue.text: Going up some ski-run, ignoring last member in order

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: part means some of something

indicators.note: ignoring last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a piste is a prepared ski run

explanation.surface: A skier climbing part of a slope without the last person in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a monk of the Cistercian order of strict observance.

clue.text: Place for growing conspiracy among tennis players?

indicators.note: among says the scheme belongs among the ranked players, so their word leads

parts.note: seeds are the ranked players in a tennis tournament draw
a plot is a secret scheme

explanation.surface: Somewhere to grow things, or a scheme hatched among the top players at a tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, seeds are the top-ranked players, kept apart in the draw; 'tennis players?' with its question mark flags that unusual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedbed or nursery patch is ground where seedlings are raised.

clue.text: Peer through this, swapping LP in crafty expectation

indicators.note: swapping LP says the letters L and P trade places, L giving way to P in the crafty word

parts.note: sly means crafty

indicators.note: in points to the second word, where the reverse exchange happens, P giving way to L

parts.note: hope is an expectation

explanation.surface: A peephole viewer looks through, while a cunning record is swapped in hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping LP' exchanges the L of SLY and the P of HOPE, giving SPY and HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peephole in a door is a small opening to look through.

clue.text: French statesman and artist, almost ignoring outsiders, pulled together

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Degas was a French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: ignoring outsiders means dropping the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A French leader and a painter, nearly excluding foreigners, joined forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle led Free France and became President of the Fifth Republic.

clue.text: States name adopted by part of road in French town

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a lane is a division of a road
USA, the United States

explanation.surface: A town in France takes its name from an American road.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray '7'; the printed page has no number there.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city on Lake Geneva, French-speaking though in Switzerland.

clue.text: Unlucky today?

parts.note: a date thought to bring bad luck

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether today is a bad day.
explanation.definitionFit: The number thirteen is superstitiously unlucky, so this day of the month may be.

clue.text: Leaving the company?

parts.note: read not as quitting an employer but as getting away from other people's company, to be by oneself

explanation.surface: Someone handing in their notice at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' looks like a business; it means being with other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alone, without companions, has left all company behind.

clue.text: Rodent, not indoors, a soldier's seen around

indicators.note: the soldier is seen placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier
out means away from home, not inside

explanation.surface: A rodent that has escaped from the house, and a soldier spotted nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a long-legged burrowing rodent of Central and South America.

clue.text: Happen to be taken short, and long to be a resident

indicators.note: taken short means cut off before its end, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: to occur is to happen
to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A tenant desperate for the toilet who also yearns to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' (British slang for urgently needing a toilet) cuts the R from OCCUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a house is its occupier or inhabitant.

clue.text: Maybe overseas firm wasted a million — I'm backing out

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged
backing out means withdrawing, so the letters of I'm are taken out of the jumble

explanation.surface: A company has squandered a million, and the speaker is pulling out of the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: an overseas territory may be colonial. 'wasted' and 'backing out' together make a composite anagram: the clue words minus I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonial possessions were territories governed from abroad, so an overseas territory may be colonial.

clue.text: Where men may find mates

parts.note: men are pieces in a board game and mate is checkmate, not friends or partners

explanation.surface: Somewhere a man might meet a partner or a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' and 'mates' look social; they are game pieces and checkmates.
explanation.definitionFit: The chequered board of sixty-four squares is the field on which kings are checkmated.

clue.text: Review of movie cut from free issue

indicators.note: cut from means taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to emancipate is to set free

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking at it again backwards

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a movie

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a film edited out of a free newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review of' turns PIC into CIP, and 'cut from' removes it from EMANCIPATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or come forth from a source.

clue.text: Muscle in as kidnapper swaps first of boys for daughter

indicators.note: swaps here means one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: an abductor is a kidnapper

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of boys

explanation.surface: A strongman playing a kidnapper takes a girl instead of the boys.
explanation.definitionFit: An adductor is a muscle that draws a limb towards the body's midline.

clue.text: On three occasions, left a few vowels out in song of praise

indicators.note: out means laid out, the letters spread among one another

parts.note: L for left, taken three times
a handful of vowels: A, E, U, I and A

explanation.surface: Singing a hymn, someone drops vowels three times.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Ls are spread out among the vowels A, E, U, I, A; the clue gives no strict order.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleluia is a Hebrew cry meaning praise the Lord, used in hymns.

clue.text: A question of placing woman's English — be first to grasp it

indicators.note: grasp means hold within, so the winning word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to win is to come first
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle about where to put a woman's English, urging someone to grab it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link pointing back to HER and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherein asks in what place or respect, so it is a question about location.

clue.text: Computer facility died twice — one's called in to listen

indicators.note: called in means brought inside, so these letters go within the listening word

parts.note: hark means to listen

indicators.note: twice means the letter for died appears two times

parts.note: one's is I's, read as I plus S

explanation.surface: A computer crashed twice, and someone is summoned to hear about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard disk is a computer's built-in storage device.

clue.text: Give up, ringing about when to change duties

indicators.note: ringing about means encircling, so the resign word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to resign is to give up
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Someone quits, phoning round about when a job reshuffle will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign someone is to give them a different task or post.

clue.text: Nominate science fiction epic you originally trashed

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A critic picks out a sci-fi blockbuster that was savaged by reviewers.
explanation.definitionFit: To specify is to name or state something explicitly.

clue.text: Part of flower representing Scot in his place of birth, possibly

indicators.note: in places the Scot inside the town

parts.note: Perth is a Scottish city, a plausible birthplace for a Scot
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A botanical term illustrated by a Scotsman in his home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' is a link. PERTH is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The perianth is the outer envelope of a flower, made up of its calyx and corolla together.

clue.text: Wander about excessively, getting let off?

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who roams too much is excused punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to go along in a leisurely, aimless way.

clue.text: Typically unfair description of a woman

definitions.text: Typically unfair description of a woman

parts.words: Typically unfair description of a woman
parts.note: unfair read literally as not fair-haired, so a dark-haired woman is by definition not fair

explanation.surface: A complaint about sexist descriptions of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfair' looks like injustice; it means not blonde.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair is the opposite of a fair-haired blonde.

clue.text: Cunning, but wrong way to put fault right

indicators.note: put the wrong way means arranged incorrectly, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A sly person suggests a misguided method for correcting a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful means crafty or wily, skilled in deceit.

clue.text: Start single egg I had

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is single
a nit is the egg of a louse
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: Someone recalling beginning the day with one egg for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it or set it going.

clue.text: Stick around with excursion, joining on near the back

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for stick is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick
a sally is a trip or outing

explanation.surface: Advice to keep to the path with a group on a walk, staying near the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsal means relating to the back, so dorsally is positioned on or towards the back.

clue.text: Snoopy character tended to lie, on top of this

definitions.text: Snoopy character tended to lie, on top of this

parts.words: Snoopy character tended to lie, on top of this
parts.note: Snoopy, the cartoon beagle in Peanuts, famously lies on the roof of his doghouse

explanation.surface: A nosy person was inclined to tell untruths about this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snoopy' looks like nosy and 'lie' like untruth; it is the dog lying on his home.
explanation.definitionFit: A doghouse or dog shelter is where a pet dog sleeps.
